etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English avys, from Old French avis, from the phrase ce m'est a vis ("in my view"), where vis is from Latin visus, past participle of videre (“to see”). See vision, and compare avise, advise. The unhistoric -d- was introduced in English 15c. Doublet of aviso.

Displaced native Old English rǣd.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) An opinion offered to guide behavior in an effort to be helpful.

quote.text: We may give advice, but we can not give conduct.

quote.citation: c. 1590–1591 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Two Gentlemen of Verona”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, (please specify the act number in uppercase Roman numerals, and the scene number in lowercase Roman numerals):
quote.text: How shall I dote on her with more advice, That thus without advice begin to love her?

definitions.definition: (archaic, commonly in plural) Information or news given; intelligence
(countable) In language about financial transactions executed by formal documents, an advisory  document.

quote.citation: 1990, United States Office of the Federal Register, The Code of Federal Regulations of the United States of America:
quote.text: (g) A Reserve Bank will issue to each depositor following any transaction affecting book-entry securities maintained for such depositor under this part a confirmation thereof in the form of an advice (serially numbered or otherwise) which shall describe the amount and maturity date thereof, and include pertinent transaction data.

quote.citation: 1992, Benjamin Geva, The Law of Electronic Funds Transfers - Issue 3:
quote.text: However, an advice of an incoming settlement payment order will be given to an off-line receiving bank only when the receiving bank has notified the Reserve Bank in writing

definitions.definition: (uncountable) In commercial language, information communicated by letter; used chiefly in reference to drafts or bills of exchange

quote.citation: 1884, John Proffatt, Abraham Clark Freeman, The American Decisions […] :
quote.text: the drawees acknowledged the receipt of the letter of advice of the nineteenth of December , and promised to honor the draft when presented

definitions.definition: (countable, law) A communication providing information, such as how an uncertain area of law might apply to possible future actions

quote.citation: 1992, Robert M. MacLean, European Community Law Textbook:
quote.text: Any measure that is not a formal (binding) act within the meaning of article 189 EEC, such as for example an advice, is clearly outside the scope of the action.

quote.citation: 1999, J. Vervaele, Compliance and Enforcement of European Community Law:
quote.text: the question arises, whether an advice issued by a Monitoring Committee would actually be applicable in a Dutch court
the Executive Director will determine which requests will be referred to chief counsel for preparation of an advice and which requests will be submitted directly to the Commission for an opinion.

quote.citation: 1996, Valerie Beardsmore, Opinion Writing & Drafting In Tort:
quote.text: The central purpose of this chapter is, however, to explain how to write an advice or an opinion.

Documents and submissions to the Commission relating to a request for an opinion or an appeal of an advice shall be made at least 7 days prior to the meeting of the Commission during which the appeal or opinion will be reviewed

definitions.definition: (uncountable, law) Counseling to perform a specific legal act.

quote.citation: 1885, Francis Wharton, A Treatise on the Criminal Law of the United States:
quote.text: An honest oath taken under advice of counsel, therefore, is not perjury

definitions.definition: (uncountable, law) Counseling to perform a specific illegal act.
(countable, programming) In aspect-oriented programming, the code whose execution is triggered when a join point is reached.
